children: dropped 5.2%, falling for a third straight day, as investors wait for an update on its planned $500 million sale to Western Union
Shares of Intermex have declined 11% this week on no new apparent news. The stock is now trading at the lowest since Aug. 13, the day before a New York regulator

in what investors initially thought was the final approval needed for the deal to close. The companies also announced on the same day that they received a letter from the California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation suspending the approval extension previously granted on July 31.
Some people have told Seeking Alpha that Western Union
has been conducting some meetings with investors this week, and that may be the reason for Intermex's decline.
Western Union and Intermex didn't immediately respond to Seeking Alpha's email request for comment.
